title: After 2023, "forest" means something narrower on paper
sources: Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 (Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 as amended), Section 1A(1)
T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India, Supreme Court, 12 December 1996
Supreme Court order, 19 February 2024, W.P.(C) 1164/2023 (Ashok Kumar Sharma v. Union of India), sci.gov.in
Supreme Court order, 4 March 2025: earlier directions remain in force
Supreme Court hearing, 16 September 2026: will examine constitutional validity of the 2023 definition (PTI via Nagaland Post; Verdictum)

quiz.q: Under Godavarman, what meaning does forest take?
options: Only land notified under forest laws
Only land owned by the government
quiz.why: Right. In Godavarman (1996) the Supreme Court held that 'forest' is to be understood in its dictionary sense, irrespective of ownership or classification.

right.label: 2023 law
right.text: Notified, or recorded as forest since 25 October 1980

claims.claim: Godavarman (1996): the Forest Conservation Act applies to all forests irrespective of ownership or classification; 'forest' is understood in its dictionary meaning

Section 1A(1) of the amended Act (2023) covers land declared or notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 or other law, and land recorded in Government record as forest on or after 25 October 1980
Unrecorded 'deemed' forest land may fall outside the amended definition (ThePrint estimates about 15% of forest cover)
claims.quote: about 1.97 lakh square kilometers would stand excluded

claims.claim: On 19 February 2024 the Supreme Court directed that the Godavarman principles continue to be observed pending the Rule 16 exercise by States/UTs (record of forest-like areas)
On 16 September 2026 the Supreme Court said it will examine the constitutional validity of the 2023 definition of forest; the challenge is pending

review_note: Spec written after the fact for the existing video and Sarvam recording; spoken text matches 21-forest-definition.voice.txt word for word (Sarvam text says 'Godavarman'; the older ElevenLabs script spelled it out for pronunciation). Claims copied from the claims table. Claims 1, 2 and 4 rest on the Supreme Court order of 19 Feb 2024 (primary). Claim 3: ThePrint (403 here, not reopened) plus the same order, which records the petitioners' submission that about 1.97 of 7.13 lakh sq km of forest would be excluded; that is a submission, not a finding, and it does not match ThePrint's 15% figure, which is not shown on screen. Claim 5 now has a second source: Verdictum (16 Sept 2026, opened) confirms the bench will confine itself to the validity of the 2023 definition. Kept neutral: no view on whether the Act dilutes protection. The chain on screen says 'September 2026', matching the narration. gsPaper adds prelims-gs.
